title: N1: one request through an LLM server (new lesson t0.l7, read second)
what: A 15-minute lesson read right after t0.l1 on the full ramp and on serving-first. It teaches what happens to one chat request: text becomes tokens, prefill reads the prompt once, the decode loop makes one token per step, K and V are kept so earlier tokens are never recomputed, TTFT and ITL are the two waits the user feels, and a batch shares each weight read across requests. It is built round an interaction, not prose: the learner steps one request token by token and predicts, before each reveal, which number moves (time to first token, the gap between tokens, the KV bytes held), then adds a second request and predicts what batching does to each. The numbers come from Boot's claims (BOOT_CLAIMS: H100 bandwidth, Llama-3-8B parameters, KV bytes per token), so every figure is a registry claim. The lesson links each stage to Capstone Zero's steps (tokenize, forward, decode, kv-cache, batch). Later lessons that lean on it: t0.l1's reveal (after K1-7), t0.l5 'TTFT pays', t2.l3 'TTFT/ITL cliff', t4.l2's KV heads, and t5.l1 and t5.l3, whose definitions become one-line recaps that point back (edited here). Standard: Boot (the learner computes on sourced numbers) and the t5.l7 play's debrief. It carries new T0 KCs with requires edges, a ticket (every T0 lesson has one), prequestions, and a quiz with a reason per option under the verify-items ratchet. It fills the slot t0.l7 that K1-5 reserves, after the release; public counts come from K1-5's derived number.

title: Pre-register and backtest the tag re-read before any tool exists
findings: section 7 Wave 3 (re-read the 108 tag-pinned claims; backtest first)
what: docs/prereg/tag-reread.md in the form of docs/prereg/watcher.md, which the owner signed on 2026-10-14 and whose rule this follows: "A better matcher is a new matcher: it is scored on a new window, rated again, under a new pre-registration." The question is narrower than the dropped watcher's: is a sentence the course already asserts still true at the project's newest release? Unit: a (pinned claim, later release tag) pair. Flag rule, frozen before scoring: the claim's quote is not found exactly once, after whitespace normalisation, in the file its source URL names with pin.ref replaced by the later tag, or that file is gone. Inputs, frozen with sha256: the 39 claims pinned to GitHub refs (vllm 18, sglang 8, InferenceX 8, BurstGPT 3, EPLB 1, triton 1) as they stood at d478f91, before Wave 0's re-pin; their quoted files at every release tag from v0.31.0 to v0.34.0 of vLLM and the same dates for the other repos; and the same files at the tags in docs/backtest/snapshot.json's window (vLLM v0.27.0 to v0.30.0, SGLang v0.5.17 to v0.5.20), stepped forward from the oldest tag where each quote exists. The 69 Hugging Face config claims are re-read at their repository's newest revision and reported apart. Truth: a blind rater (the owner, or a fresh agent that only the owner or the orchestrator launches, as watcher.md requires) reads each pair's file and says whether the claim's value and boundary still hold, never seeing the flags. Scoring script refuses an unsigned file, as scripts/landscape/score.ts does. Proposed keep bar, stated here before any rating: (1) production.vllm.block-size is flagged at v0.34.0 whenever the rater marks it changed (the report: "It should flag the block size"); (2) recall at least 0.80 on rated-changed pairs; (3) precision at least 0.50, since a flag is one quote in one file, not a release-note line; (4) at most 15 flags a week averaged over the span; (5) at least 5 rated-changed pairs, else underpowered and repeated on the next releases. Reported and not part of the bar: how many of the 44 lines docs/backtest/ratings.json rates true the re-read would have caught; none of those 44 names a claim id, so the expected answer is few or none, which says the re-read cannot replace the manual release-note scan.

risk: Quote-not-found is not fact-changed: reformatting and moved files give false flags, and a default changed by a platform override elsewhere (the block-size case may be one) leaves the quote in place and misses. The backtest exists to measure exactly that; no threshold moves after numbers are known.
done_when: The pre-registration, frozen snapshot with its sha256, flag script and scoring script are merged; the scoring script refuses to write a report while the Signed line is empty and refuses a ratings file carrying flag fields; a unit test reproduces the flag rule on recorded fixtures; after signing and rating, docs/backtest/tag-reread/report.json states keep, drop or underpowered by the five bars.

title: Generator families for T0 and T1: bytes, lines and addresses
what: Two families in the existing framework (Gen with kcs, make(seed, level), grade, solution; lures that name the slip; the level 0-3 fade; staircase), each pinned to its lesson's own worked example. `lines` (T0): cache lines fetched by a loop at a given stride; bytes moved for row-major against column-major traversal of an N x N matrix; useful bytes per line for AoS against SoA; time on the ladder from lines x latency. Lures: counted elements not lines; forgot the line size; used the wrong ladder rung. `addr` (T1): what p + k advances in bytes for a typed pointer; a frame's offsets from rsp for a given call; header plus payload alignment. And the ladder numbers the course calls reflexive (latency ladder, 3.35 TB/s, 2 FLOPs per parameter) as `fact` KCs so review brings the numbers back. KC wiring: `gen` on t0.cache-lines, t0.stride-traversal, t0.data-layout, t0.latency-ladder and on the T1 pointer and frame KCs. T0 goes from 0 of 10 KCs generated to about 4; T1 from 4 of 14 to about 7.
risk: A wrong number served at scale on fresh seeds; the property tests and cue-ablation QA K1 requires are the guard. The families must take their constants from the lessons after W1's O12 (one DRAM bandwidth across T0's simulators) or they will pin the old numbers. Read as continuing K1 (the plan's metric is '>=70% of KCs generated'), not as 'K1 v2', which PLAN-100X gates to 2027-11.
done_when: verify:generators passes with the two families and their hash fixtures; verify:kc reports the new coverage for T0 and T1; each variant has a worked level-0 instance equal to its lesson's example; every lure's diagnosis is covered by a test; bun run test green; /today bundle within its gate (verify:bundle).
